sectors: Breadth was strong (S&P advancers 319 vs 184 decliners). Health care and biotech led (Humana, Moderna, Novavax), tower REITs surged, and gold/silver miners rose, while wireless carriers collapsed on the SpaceX spectrum news. Oil eased after President Trump said the US would not strike Iran before the midterms (Brent down more than 1% but still above $100), and the 10-year Treasury yield held roughly flat near 5.24% after a 24-year high of about 5.37% on Wednesday.
weekText: For the week ending Oct 9 the S&P 500 rose 1.2%, the Dow 0.9% and the Nasdaq 0.6% (fourth straight weekly gain for the Nasdaq). The S&P 500 set a record close on Tuesday Oct 6 and finished Friday just below it.
recap: Stocks rallied Friday Oct 9 to close out a volatile week higher: the Dow rose 423 points (0.8%) to 51,655, the S&P 500 0.6% to 7,812 (just shy of Tuesday's record) and the Nasdaq 0.6% to 27,366. Oil pulled back and Treasury yields stabilized after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms. The big story was telecom: T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon fell 9-13% after SpaceX bought about $8B of spectrum to launch Starlink Mobile, while tower REITs (Crown Castle, American Tower, SBA), Humana (Medicare Advantage ratings) and Moderna (Nasdaq-100 inclusion) jumped. Attention turns to bank earnings (JPM, GS, WFC, C on Tue Oct 13) and September CPI this week.
